resources.string: The time, and what comes next.
Every calendar the phone already has, from every account. Nothing to sign in to, nothing to sync.
Tempo reads your events and never writes them: creating and changing one stay in your calendar app. It has no internet permission at all.
No service, no polling. Tempo works while you look, or when your calendar changes, and never on a timer.
To show your day, Tempo needs to read the phone’s calendar. It reads the events of the days it shows, on the phone, and nothing else: no contacts, no location, no internet.
Without it, the clock and the date still work, and you can allow it later from Today or from Settings.
Two widgets. Their clock is drawn by Android itself, right to the minute, at no cost to the battery.
The time and the date over the rest of your day, never a list to scroll.
A clock face with what comes next on its ring, and the day in a few words.
To add one, touch and hold an empty spot on the home screen, choose Widgets, then Tempo.
A Tempo widget is on your home screen. Touch and hold it to change what it shows and how it looks.
